options.B: Industry includes more than manufacturing, so the industry-sector contribution is broader than the manufacturing-sector contribution

questions.explanation: Do not confuse industry-sector contribution with manufacturing-sector contribution. Industry includes more than manufacturing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which node is correctly matched with its industrial corridor?

options.B: Tumakuru - Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor; Dharwad - Bengaluru-Mumbai Industrial Corridor

questions.explanation: Tumakuru is the Karnataka node under CBIC; Dharwad is identified under BMIC planning. Orvakal is in Andhra Pradesh under HBIC.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: In which state is Orvakal, the identified node under the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor?

options.B: Telangana

questions.explanation: Orvakal is in Andhra Pradesh. It is the identified node under HBIC, not a Karnataka node.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: What is the difference between software exports and merchandise exports?

options.B: Software exports are services exports, while merchandise exports are goods exports

questions.explanation: Do not confuse software exports with merchandise exports; software exports are services exports.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: What is the difference between aerospace and automobile manufacturing?

options.B: Aerospace covers aircraft and space-related products, while automobiles cover road vehicles and components

questions.explanation: Do not confuse aerospace with automobile manufacturing: aerospace covers aircraft and space-related products, while automobiles cover road vehicles and components.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: What is the nature of the targets under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30, such as ₹7.5 lakh crore investment and 20 lakh jobs?

options.B: They are intended outcomes or targets, not completed achievements

questions.explanation: Targets under a policy are intended outcomes, not completed achievements. For example, ₹7.5 lakh crore investment and 20 lakh jobs are targets under the 2025-30 Industrial Policy.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: What is the primary source for the latest industry facts in the notes?

options.A: Reserve Bank of India Annual Report
options.B: Government of Karnataka, Economic Survey of Karnataka 2025-26, March 2026

questions.explanation: Primary source: Government of Karnataka, Economic Survey of Karnataka 2025-26, March 2026. Relevant sections include Chapter 3 - Investment and Exports and Chapter 8 - Industry.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which chapters of the Economic Survey 2025-26 are relevant for industry-related data?

options.B: Chapter 3 - Investment and Exports and Chapter 8 - Industry

questions.explanation: Relevant sections include Chapter 3 - Investment and Exports (ESDM, electronics exports, biotechnology, IT and policies) and Chapter 8 - Industry (MSMEs, manufacturing, industrial performance and aerospace policy).

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: What does the accuracy note in the source document advise regarding Economic Survey figures?

options.A: All figures are identical across sections
options.B: The Economic Survey contains different estimates and reference periods; in an exam, reproduce the figure with its stated year, price basis, estimate status and source
options.C: Only the executive summary figures should be used
options.D: Only the detailed tables should be used

questions.explanation: The Economic Survey contains different estimates and reference periods. For example, the executive summary and detailed sector tables may present distinct estimates. In an exam, reproduce the figure with its stated year, price basis, estimate status and source.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of an industrial service?

options.B: Providing logistics and warehousing support to manufacturing units

questions.explanation: Industry includes the provision of certain industrial services. Logistics and warehousing support to manufacturing units is an industrial service, whereas farming, school teaching and medical practice fall outside the industrial sector as defined.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following activities is part of the industrial sector as defined in the notes?

options.B: Electricity, gas and water supply

questions.explanation: The industrial sector is mainly associated with mining and quarrying, manufacturing, electricity, gas, water supply and construction. Banking, insurance and retail trade are part of the service sector.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following best describes a semi-finished product?

options.A: A product that is fully ready for final consumer use
options.B: A product that has undergone some processing but requires further processing before final use
options.C: A raw material extracted directly from the earth
options.D: A product that cannot be processed further

questions.explanation: Manufacturing converts raw materials or components into finished or semi-finished products. A semi-finished product has undergone some processing but requires further processing before final use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a finished product?

options.A: Iron ore extracted from a mine
options.B: A car ready for sale to consumers

questions.explanation: A finished product is one that is ready for final use or sale. A car ready for sale to consumers is a finished product; iron ore, steel slabs and cotton bales are raw or semi-finished materials.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a semi-finished product?

options.B: Steel slabs awaiting further processing

questions.explanation: A semi-finished product has undergone some processing but requires further processing before final use. Steel slabs awaiting further processing are an example.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of industrialisation?

options.B: Raising productivity

questions.explanation: Industrialisation creates jobs, raises productivity, adds value to raw materials, encourages exports, develops infrastructure, promotes technological progress and generates demand for services and supporting industries. It promotes, not reduces, technological progress.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of industrialisation?

options.B: Adding value to raw materials

questions.explanation: Industrialisation creates jobs and generates demand for services; it does not reduce employment opportunities as a benefit.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of industrialisation?

options.B: Promoting technological progress
options.D: Reducing value addition to raw materials

questions.explanation: Industrialisation adds value to raw materials; it does not reduce value addition.

questions.subject: Karnataka Industry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of industrialisation?

options.B: Creating jobs

questions.explanation: Industrialisation raises productivity; it does not reduce it.
